Do not change the system default browser or spend the action budget exploring a generic browser welcome page. steps.executor_prompt: Minimize this app, then go to the Google Voice app. If there is a Device Pin, enter {device_pin}. Navigate to the main page of Google Voice where the OTP can be found: for a mail or messaging app this is the inbox or conversation list, and for an authenticator app this is the list of accounts with their codes. Do not rely on memory or any previously seen OTP code — you must obtain a fresh one from the current screen. If it is the detailed page of a message, go back to the main inbox. If the app shows a list of messages or emails, refresh it (e.g. swipe down from the top), wait 3 seconds for it to load, check the Default Browser and go to epicgames.com/id/login, then open the newest item at the top and read the OTP code inside it. If the app directly displays rotating codes, find the entry corresponding to Default Browser and go to epicgames.com/id/login and read its currently displayed code; if that code is about to expire, wait for it to rotate and read the new one. Report that OTP code as your final answer.

Read a fresh six-digit code from the matching Evernote entry in Google Authenticator. Open Android Overview/Recents with the reliable system overview control and select the existing browser task containing the accounts.evernote.com two-factor challenge; do not launch a new browser task. If an unrelated overlay or app opens, dismiss it and recover to Authenticator or Overview instead of stopping, then read a new code if necessary. Verify the Evernote domain, enter the code in the normal six-digit authenticator field, submit it, and wait for authenticated Evernote content or an explicit login-success confirmation. Never use the backup-code field. If the code expires or is rejected, repeat the Authenticator-to-browser round trip with a fresh code.
